<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/embedder-openai`, `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **24** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-knowledge/package.json`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), documentedMaxBatchSize (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via batchSize (symbol, a field of type EmbedderFromSettings))_
- `content/docs/frontend/data-source.mdx`  _(via batchSize (symbol, a field of type EmbedderFromSettings))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via getNamespace (symbol, a method of interface EmbedderSettingsReader))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/views.mdx`  _(via batchSize (symbol, a field of type EmbedderFromSettings))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-knowledge/package.json`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 057cedfa9b6f990a7cf322118ae33bc4460ddc65` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1d5f35c1db33fdfb0d7807319751b238e51756aa` — the merge of head `fa818f4d40749e28de09bbd747e9ca3c829f17ed` into base `057cedfa9b6f990a7cf322118ae33bc4460ddc65`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1d5f35c1db33fdfb0d7807319751b238e51756aa && git checkout 1d5f35c1db33fdfb0d7807319751b238e51756aa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 057cedfa9b6f990a7cf322118ae33bc4460ddc65 fa818f4d40749e28de09bbd747e9ca3c829f17ed && git checkout -B drift-repro 057cedfa9b6f990a7cf322118ae33bc4460ddc65 && git merge --no-ff fa818f4d40749e28de09bbd747e9ca3c829f17ed

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 057cedfa9b6f990a7cf322118ae33bc4460ddc65
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 057cedfa9b6f990a7cf322118ae33bc4460ddc65` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f329965bd6888bfae8e6901e1ca230c8f37e81f9`
Local-runs: probe — pins (a) and (b), the two ablations, the env-override and key-leak readings and the ObjectKernel phase reading could only be measured by running vitest at this head, in a throwaway worktree that is now removed

### ① Derived judgments

- PR #37265 for card #37094, epic #37000, seat direction 7156326561 (option A). 21 files, +695/−5. Opened by the seat on the maintainer's authorization; the dev's facts are in the PR body.
- `record-recognisers --template --paths` refuses to pick a face from the paths (no schema, no governed path) and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line: `yes (widening)` ⇒ declaration face, `TIER_DEFAULT`.
- Check-runs at this head, read 2026-11-25T09:49Z: 62 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed, 0 running. The skipped ones are opt-in or queue-only jobs (18.x upgrade harness, packed-tarball smoke, the two queue verdicts, the schedule gate, Temporal Conformance, UI Published Artifacts, Dogfood Verify CLI, one Dogfood matrix placeholder).
- `landing-k --pr 37265` against origin/main `376377cc0c54`: K = 4, OK; no new locale pack under this label PR; no shared book moved. `git merge-tree` against that main is clean (tree `0e04038d1aab`). Main moved `pnpm-lock.yaml` after the merge-base; it merges clean.
- Local at this head: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` exit 0 (the lockfile agrees with the manifests); dependency closure built; `knowledge-settings-contribution.test.ts -t 37094` 11/11; service-knowledge 8 files, 181/181; embedder-openai 31/31.
- Pin (a), saved 64 on `text-embedding-v3` → 10, 10, 5 and the boot line names the saved 64: green. Pin (b), saved 50 on a custom model → 50, 10: green. The explicit `maxBatchSize: 25` on a cap-10 model still sends 25, 5: green.
- Ablation, clamp removed (`Math.min(savedBatch, documentedCap)` → `savedBatch`): 1 failed / 10 passed, exactly pin (a). Matches the body. Restored.
- Ablation, manifest default counted as saved (`if (!entry) return undefined;`): 11 passed, 0 failed. It does NOT match the body, which reports 1 failed / 8 passed. See S2.
- Phase, read in `packages/core/src/kernel.ts` (lines 618 to 642) and `lite-kernel.ts` (lines 146 to 156): both kernels await every `kernel:ready` handler, then dispatch `kernel:bootstrapped`, then `kernel:listening`; all three propagate a throw. `plugin-lifecycle-events.ts` says the same. So a registration in `init()`, `start()` or any `kernel:ready` handler is visible to this hook whatever the plugin order.
- "Already registered → kept": `init` and `kernel:ready` are pinned on LiteKernel. On ObjectKernel I measured by probe: an async factory is kept (`Service 'embedder' is async - use await` is not the not-found message, so it reads as registered; one `info` line, no id); nothing registered → the placeholder; a registration in a later `kernel:bootstrapped` handler fails the boot with `[Kernel] Service 'embedder' already registered`, as the changeset warns.
- API key: the pin is in the first #37094 case (`lines.filter((l) => l.line.includes(API_KEY))` is empty), which covers the log lines of the configured path. By reading, no log line and no error built in this diff interpolates the key: the boot lines carry provider, model and batch size; the refusal reasons carry the page check's message, the settings read error or the embedder's constructor error, none of which holds the key. By probe: a saved key with incomplete settings, and a provider answering 401, put the key in no log line and no error text. `OpenAIEmbedder`'s own request errors carry the base URL, the status and 200 characters of the response body, not the key.
- i18n: `ai.keys.embedder_provider.help` is present in all 11 bundles (ar, de, en, es-ES, fr, ja-JP, ko, pt-BR, ru, zh-CN, zh-Hant); the `en` text equals the manifest `description`.
- Dependency edge: `embedder-openai` depends on `spec` only; `service-settings` depends on neither of the other two; no cycle. `check:workspace-manifest-cycles` is green in CI.
- Overlap, of the open PRs only #37256 touches a file of this diff (`knowledge-service-plugin.ts`: one import and one constructor option in `init()`). `git merge-tree` of the two heads is clean. #37098 has no PR yet.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` holds: `documentedMaxBatchSize(model): number | undefined` is a new export of a published package, nothing is removed or tightened, and it is named in the body and in the changeset as the direction required.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: the diff adds a `description` to one existing specifier of the platform's own `ai` manifest and its `help` copy. No key, accepted value, default or metadata type changes for an author.
- `patch` on service-knowledge, service-settings and embedder-openai is the level AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 gives: `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`.
- `OpenAIEmbedder` is unchanged for a caller, with one edge: the constructor now reads the table through `hasOwnProperty`, so a model named like an `Object.prototype` key (`constructor`) falls back to 10 where it used to take a function as its batch size. A correction, pinned.
- The changeset carries the migration sentence for a host that registers the name after `kernel:ready`. That is the one behaviour change for an existing host; see S3.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Seat direction 7156326561, all four conditions met: the body reads `Clause-②: yes` and names the export; the changeset names it and says an explicit `maxBatchSize` is unchanged; a pin reddens when the clamp goes (re-measured); a second pin keeps an unknown model's saved size.
- Declared beyond the named surface: the vitest alias and the lockfile entry are both mechanically forced. Accepted.
- "Search reports, it does not throw": accepted. The catch is in `knowledge-service.ts`, outside the diff; the logged error is the named reason (pinned).
- "No open-edition adapter consumes `EMBEDDER_SERVICE` yet": confirmed, no other reader of the name exists under `packages/`.
- The stale `EMBEDDER_SERVICE` doc comment in spec: N1.
- Saved versus default: `savedValue` returns a value only when `source` is not `default`, so an `OS_*` override (`source: 'env'`) counts. The completeness check is handed the `saved` map only; its payload is empty, so nothing unsaved reaches it. The map holds every saved `ai` key, not only the embedder ones (N5). The handler sends no request (read, and pinned by the zero-request assertions).
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no query in this diff.

### ④ Design judgment

- M1 (must-fix) — a credential-handling defect in how saved embedder settings are applied. Under the security-findings rules its mechanism is not recorded here; the finding and the required fix and pin were handed to the dev through the zone's dispatch. Closure is read at the next head.
- S1 (should-fix) — an `OS_AI_EMBEDDER_DIMENSIONS` override is dropped without a line. The key has no default, so the settings service hands the env value over as a string (`"256"`, `source: 'env'`); `typeof saved.embedder_dimensions === 'number'` is false; the embedder reports the model's default (measured: 1536) and sends no `dimensions`. An adapter then sizes its column from the wrong number. The body says an `OS_*` override counts as saved. Asked: accept a numeric string for the two number keys, or refuse it at `warn`; one case.
- S2 (should-fix) — the saved-versus-default reading has no pin at this head, and the body's ablation line for it is stale. Since the clamp commit, a default 64 counted as saved is clamped to 10 on `text-embedding-v3`, the same 10, 10, 5 the case expects, so the mutation is green. The difference shows only on a model with no documented cap: measured, 70 inputs on `my-gateway-model` with no saved batch size send 10 × 7 at head and 64, 6 under the mutation. Asked: that case, and the body's ablation line corrected.
- S3 (should-fix) — the cloud ordering claim is NOT MEASURED. The cloud source is not readable from this session (repository access was refused), so "cloud registers before `kernel:bootstrapped`" rests on the body alone. What this repository does say (`packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md`, entry 4f9e9d4): `service-ai` builds its embedder in `bindSettings()`, leaves the service unset when the provider is `none`, and on `settings:changed` "registers / replaces" it without a restart. With this PR a deployment that mounts the knowledge service and boots with no embedder has the placeholder under the name. If cloud's hot path calls `registerService` when it holds no embedder of its own, it now throws `already registered`; if it calls `replaceService`, it works. And if `bindSettings()` runs later than `kernel:ready`, the boot fails as measured above. Asked of the seat before landing: one reading in cloud of the phase `bindSettings()` runs in and of the call its hot path makes, recorded on the PR.
- N1 — the `EMBEDDER_SERVICE` doc comment in `packages/spec/src/contracts/embedder.ts` still says the service is registered by `service-ai` and may be absent. A follow-up outside this surface.
- N2 — the restart help is shown wherever the embedder section is, also where another plugin's embedder is kept and may apply changes without a restart.
- N3 — any `getService` error other than not-found reads as "already registered", and the `info` line then says so. Right for an async factory; wider than the comment states.
- N4 — the async-factory keep and the ObjectKernel path have no case; every #37094 case boots LiteKernel.
- N5 — the completeness check is handed every saved `ai` key, chat provider keys included. It reads only `embedder_*`; the map could be narrowed to that prefix.
- N6 — the API-key pin asserts the configured path's log lines only; the same assertion on the incomplete case and on a provider error would pin what the body claims for errors.
- For the second lander of this file set (#37098, #37256): keep the `documentedMaxBatchSize` export and the constructor reading the table through it; keep the `kernel:bootstrapped` hook above the `enableEventSync` early return in `start()`, `provideEmbedder` and both import hunks; keep `embedder_provider.description` in `ai.manifest.ts` and `embedder_provider.help` in all 11 bundles (the coverage test reddens a described field with no `help`).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37094-open-embedder-settings`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYpEsWWE9Y5YtSsDgqZ`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
